steps.name: Blend the blue wall

lines.text: Rinse the brush well first. Dirty water tints every color with the last one.
Inside the outlined area, all the way across from the top edge. Its bottom is about 6 in from the bottom edge.
The outline also runs under where the yellow knit blanket and the wooden windowsill will go: paint straight through there.
Paints, top to bottom: Wall blue, then Deep wall blue.
Brush: 1 inch wide flat. Load: Creamy paint. An even coat.
Start with the darkest color and stroke side to side. Without rinsing, pick up the next lighter color and paint below it. Then stroke back up over the join several times.
It should leave smooth bands of color, with a soft join where two wet colors meet.
Watch out: Blending after the paint has started to drag. Acrylic sets in minutes, and scrubbing setting paint lifts it and leaves streaks. Fix: stop as soon as it drags.
Let it dry, then blend a new thin layer on top.

steps.meant: Everything right of the window is a smooth blue wall, deeper blue by the window, softer to the right. The window view is untouched; no frame, sill, blanket or cat yet.

steps.name: Block in the window frame

lines.text: Let the blue wall dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Rinse the brush well first. Dirty water tints every color with the last one.
Optional: lightly chalk its outline first, from the transfer outline in Before you start, measuring from the canvas edges with a ruler.
Inside the outlined area. Its top is at the top edge, and its left side is at the left edge; it's about 4 in wide and 8 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the yellow knit blanket and the wooden windowsill will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the blue wall, painted already: there, only soften this paint into its edge and leave it showing.
Paint: Warm white.
Brush: 1/2 inch flat.
Start with one simple shape (an oval, a circle, or a rectangle). Then add the rest in curved pieces on each side, like ( ), smaller toward the edges.
It should leave a shape made of distinct curved segments with small gaps or overlaps between them.
Warm white is much lighter than what it goes over: expect two or three thin coats, letting each dry.

steps.meant: A flat cream-white window frame (posts, crossbar and bottom ledge) stands over the window view and the wall's left edge, with no shading. Sill, blanket and cat are not there yet.

steps.name: Shade the frame's inner sides

lines.text: Let the white window frame and the blue wall dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its top is at the top edge, and its left side is at the left edge; it's about 4 1/2 in wide and 8 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the yellow knit blanket and the wooden windowsill will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the blue wall, painted already: there, only soften this paint into its edge and leave it showing.
Paint: Lavender gray.
Brush: 1/4 inch flat.
Start with one simple shape (an oval, a circle, or a rectangle). Then add the rest in curved pieces on each side, like ( ), smaller toward the edges.
It should leave a shape made of distinct curved segments with small gaps or overlaps between them.
Step back, squint, or take a photo to see it whole, and compare the big shapes with the picture.

steps.meant: The window frame is finished: cream white with lavender shadow bands on its inner sides. Sill, blanket and cat are not there yet.
